 Los Angeles Lakers will face their next challenge against the Charlotte Hornets with two important absences in their starting lineup. Austin Reaves , due to a contusion on his left heel, and Walker Kessler , due to discomfort in the lower part of his leg, will be unavailable for the match this Tuesday, as confirmed by the franchise itself. 
 Reaves' absence will mark his second consecutive game off the court. However, JJ Redick offered relatively positive news about his recovery last Sunday, stating that the guard is progressing well and that his return will primarily depend on how well he tolerates the pain. Only Luka Doncic remains. 
 "He is improving. Really, it all comes down to pain tolerance. There's nothing structural beyond a contusion, so I think each day he has been getting better," explained the Lakers' coach. 
 Kessler's situation also presents a setback for Los Angeles. The center is having a remarkable start to the season, averaging 14.5 points, a 68% shooting accuracy, 10.9 rebounds, and 2.2 blocks per game. Additionally, he was one of the three players on the roster who had played in the previous 14 games for the Lakers. 
 His consistency has been particularly important for a team that has started the season at an extraordinary level, with a record of 12 wins and only two losses. Now, Redick will have to manage two significant absences at a demanding time in the schedule. 
 A demanding schedule for the Lakers 
 The matchup against Charlotte will be the first of two consecutive games for the Lakers, who will host the Utah Jazz on Wednesday, precisely Kessler's former team. Furthermore, the game against the Hornets will be the second in a sequence of three games in four days. 
 The Angelenos arrive at this meeting after securing an important away victory against the Phoenix Suns by 131-123 last Sunday. A win that confirmed their good form, although the accumulated fatigue and the two absences will force the team to seek alternatives. 
 The big question will be how long Reaves and Kessler will need to recover. In Reaves' case, Redick's latest statements point to a favorable progression, while no specific timeline for the return of either player has been provided yet.
